en: When psychiatrists refer to déjà vu, they do not mean a known event of the past playing out again, accompanied by either euphoric amazement or bored condescension. Rather, here we have an only apparent repetition, one that is entirely illusory. We believe that we have already experienced (or seen, heard, done, etc.) something that is, in fact, happening for the first time at this very moment. We mistake the current experience for the very faithful copy of an original that never really existed. We believe that we are recognising something of which we are only now cognisant. As such, we could also describe déjà vu in terms of ‘false recognition’.
zh: 精神病学家所说的既视感，并不是过去某个已知事件再次上演，并伴随着欣喜的惊讶或厌倦的优越感。这里出现的只是表面上的重复，而且纯属幻觉。某件事情事实上正在此刻第一次发生，我们却相信自己已经经历过它（或已经见过、听过、做过，等等）。我们把当前经验误认为某个原型极其忠实的摹本，尽管那个原型从未真正存在。我们相信自己正在认出某个东西，实际上却是直到此刻才第一次认识它。因此，我们也可以把既视感称为“错误再认”（false recognition）。

en: Déjà vu does not entail a defect of memory, nor its qualitative alteration. Rather, it means the untrammelled extension of memory’s jurisdiction, of its dominion. Rather than limit itself to preserving traces of times past, memory also applies itself to actuality, to the evanescent ‘now’. The instantaneous present takes the form of memory, and is re-evoked even as it is taking place. But what can ‘remembering the present’ mean, except having the irresistible sensation of having already experienced it previously? Inasmuch as it is an object of memory, the ‘now’ is camouflaged as the already-been, and is thus duplicated in an imaginary ‘back then’, in a fictitious ‘other-then’. It goes without saying that between the

current event, considered a mere repeat, and the phantom original prototype, there is no mere analogy, but rather the most complete identity. The present and the pseudo-past, which have the same perceptual and emotional content, are indistinguishable. The consequence is a troubling one: every act and every word that I say and do
seems destined to repeat, step by step, the course that was fixed back then, without the possibility of omitting or changing anything. As Henri Bergson put it in

children: Le souvenir du présent et la fausse reconnaissance: ‘We feel that we choose

en: and will, but that we are choosing what is imposed on us and willing the inevitable.’
zh: 既视感并不意味着记忆存在缺陷，也不意味着记忆发生了质的改变。相反，它意味着记忆的管辖权、记忆的领地不受约束地扩张。记忆不再限于保存逝去岁月的痕迹，而是把当下现实、把稍纵即逝的“现在”也纳入自己的范围。瞬间的当下采取了记忆的形式，并且在它正在发生之际便被重新唤起。可是，“记住当下”除了产生一种不可抗拒的感觉，认为自己先前已经经历过当下之外，还能是什么意思？“现在”一旦成为记忆的对象，就会伪装成已经发生之物，于是它被复制到一个想象的“那时”、一个虚构的“另一个那时”之中。毋庸置疑，被看作单纯重演的当前事件与幽灵般的原初范本之间，不只是相似，而是最彻底的同一。当下与伪过去拥有相同的知觉内容和情感内容，二者无法区分。由此产生的后果令人不安：我此刻所做的每个动作、所说的每句话，似乎都注定要一步不差地重复那时已经确定的进程，不容省略，也不容改变。正如亨利·柏格森在《对当下的记忆与错误再认》中所说：“我们觉得自己正在选择、正在意愿，但我们所选择的是强加给我们的东西，我们所意愿的是不可避免之事。”

en: The state of mind correlated to déjà vu is that typical of those set on

. This means apathy, fatalism, and indifference to a future that seems prescribed even down to the last detail. Since the present is dressed in the clothes of an irrevocable past, these people must renounce any influence on how the present plays out. It is impossible to change something that has taken on the appearances of memory. As such, they give up on action. Or, better, they become

of their own actions, almost as if these were part of an already-known and unalterable script. They are dumbfounded spectators, sometimes ironic and often inclined to cynicism. The individual at the mercy of the déjà vu is her own epigone. To her eyes, the historical scansion of events is suspended or paralysed; the distinction between ‘before’ and ‘after’, cause and effect, seems futile and even derisory.
zh: 与既视感相伴的心态，典型地属于那些只顾旁观自己生活的人。这意味着冷漠、宿命论，以及对一个仿佛连最微小细节都已经写定的未来无动于衷。由于当下披上了不可撤销的过去的外衣，这些人不得不放弃对当下进程的干预。一个已经显现为记忆的东西是无法改变的。因此，他们放弃行动。或者更准确地说，他们成了自己行动的观众，仿佛那些行动只是早已熟知且不可更改的剧本的一部分。他们是目瞪口呆的观众，有时冷嘲，往往倾向于犬儒主义。任由既视感摆布的人，是她自身的迟来模仿者。在她眼中，事件的历史节奏已经中止或瘫痪；“之前”与“之后”、原因与结果之间的区别，显得徒劳，甚至可笑。

en: The phenomenon of ‘false recognition’ allows us to

decipher critically the fundamental idea of every philosophy of history: the end, the exhaustion or the implosion of history itself. Above all, it allows us to settle accounts with the contemporary – that is, ‘postmodern’ – version of this idea, which descends from a noble lineage and complicated family tree. According to Baudrillard and his miniature disciples, history thins out to the point of vanishing when the millenarian aspiration to wipe out the duration of time (and, with this, any irritating delays) appears to have been satisfied by the instantaneousness of information, real-time communications, and by the desire to lay ‘hold of things almost before they have taken place’.
And yet the affirmation of an eternal present, a centripetal and despotic
, is provoked by déjà vu, namely by the form of experience in which there prevails – as Bergson put it – ‘the feeling that
, that the situation is detached from everything although I am attached to it’.

In capricious, rampant years of history, Karl Mannheim prophesied: ‘It is possible … that in the future, in a world in which there is never anything new, in which all is finished and each moment a repetition of the past, there can exist a condition in which thought is utterly devoid of all ideological and utopian elements.’

A post-historical situation, then; but also, at the same time, a condition marked by the mnestic pathology of which we have already spoken: ‘there is never anything new … each moment [is] a repetition of the past’.
zh: “错误再认”现象使我们能够批判性地解读一切历史哲学的根本观念：历史本身的终结、耗尽或内爆。尤其重要的是，它使我们能够清算这一观念的当代版本——也就是“后现代”版本；这一版本有着高贵的血统和复杂的谱系。依照鲍德里亚及其那些小门徒的说法，当信息的瞬时性、实时通信，以及“几乎在事情发生之前就抓住它”的欲望，似乎已经满足了千百年来消除时间绵延（并同时消除一切恼人延迟）的愿望时，历史便日益稀薄，直至消失。
然而，对一个永恒当下、一个向心而专横的现实的肯定，恰恰是由既视感造成的；换句话说，是由这样一种经验形式造成的——其中占据支配地位的，正如柏格森所说，是“未来已经封闭、情境与一切相脱离而我却依附于它的感觉”。
在那些历史风云激荡、变幻莫测的年代，卡尔·曼海姆曾预言：“未来或许可能出现这样的情形……在一个从来没有任何新事物、一切都已完成、每个时刻都是过去之重复的世界里，可能存在一种思想完全不含任何意识形态和乌托邦成分的状态。”
这就是一种后历史情境；但与此同时，它也是一种带有我们已经谈到的记忆病理的状态：“从来没有任何新事物……每个时刻［都是］过去的重复。”

en: Now, however, we need to interrupt this game of assonances and analogies. To understand the increasing fragility of historical experience and, at the same time, to refute the mediocre ideologies that set up camp on this terrain, it is necessary to observe more closely the actual texture of ‘false recognition’. What clay is a
made of? How is it formed? What does it reveal?
zh: 不过，现在必须打断这种寻求呼应与类比的游戏。为了理解历史经验为何日益脆弱，同时也为了驳倒盘踞在这块地盘上的平庸意识形态，我们必须更仔细地观察“错误再认”的内在构造。对当下的记忆是用什么材料塑成的？它如何形成？它揭示了什么？
